title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering
summary: A reusable structure-conditioned renderer reduces the cost of turning diverse world proxies into observations. The renderer itself does not define world dynamics.

title: NeoWorld-3: From Pixels to Code-Defined Physical Worlds
summary: Visual observations become tunable programs with geometry, articulation and physics validation; real-robot transfer tests the operational value of reconstruction.

title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
summary: Executable game mechanics and neural observations are separated; reported key-to-display latency makes this a stronger interaction claim than video throughput alone.

title: From Code to Playable Systems: CEGame-Bench for Long-Horizon Game Creation Agents
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "CEGame-Bench", "input": "Design document + empty project across five production engines", "artifact": "Complete executable game", "checks": "Real-input play, gameplay completion, integration and saved-world behavior", "caveat": "A successful build or high integration score is insufficient for completion.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26098"}]
summary: Cross-engine game creation is judged by actual input-driven play, completion and persistence, distinguishing successful builds from playable systems.

title: LLM Agents as Suppliers of Physical System Models: Calibration and Acceptance in Modelica
summary: Multiple programs may fit the same observations; physical invariants can reject an energy-creating fit even when its data residual is small.

title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent
summary: Object structure, behavioral edits and texture memory share an object identity, connecting persistent executable state with reusable visual appearance.

title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
summary: A 3D coding corpus and verification harness connect editable assets to spatial inspection. The project reports 269,597 executable programs expanded into roughly 2.03M code–condition pairs, with 3DCodeBench evaluation splits held out; those are distinct counting units.

title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "BlenderWorld", "input": "223 tasks with text, images, videos and optional specifications", "artifact": "Editable .blend plus requested exports", "checks": "2,651 binary rubrics + multi-view holistic visual ratings", "caveat": "Broad creation coverage; not a dedicated dynamics or closed-loop physics benchmark.", "source": "https://github.com/QwenLM/BlenderWorld"}]
summary: 223 reference-driven creation tasks require editable Blender deliverables. 2,651 binary rubrics and multi-view visual ratings test instruction and structural fidelity across text, image, video and specification inputs.

title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Human and Agent Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
summary: Human and agent tools expose solver, contact-model and parameter choices for iterative real-to-sim calibration of robot manipulation.

title: Code2Worlds-2: Physically Plausible Agent Harness for Embodied World Simulation
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "SimCode4D", "input": "Five embodied task templates", "artifact": "MuJoCo-loadable scene with contacts, joints and physical attributes", "checks": "State-based physical and robot-interaction evaluation", "caveat": "Simulator compatibility should be separated from rendered appearance.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17651"}]
summary: A compiler and simulator critic turn visual 4D scenes into MuJoCo-loadable worlds with collisions, joints and contact. The key advance is operational physical semantics.

title: PhysCodeGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Physically Verifiable 4D Reconstruction
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "PhysCodeGym", "input": "156 videos across rigid, liquid, deformable and wind-driven motion", "artifact": "Executable Blender simulation", "checks": "Visual metrics, object/event rubrics, native physical measurements; 43 tasks with counterfactual checks", "caveat": "Counterfactual coverage is a subset, not a guarantee over arbitrary interventions.", "source": "https://github.com/ShaoShuai0605/PhysCodeGym"}]
summary: 156 video-to-Blender tasks combine visual metrics with program inspection and physical measurements. Counterfactual checks in 43 tasks expose contact or support defects hidden in ordinary replay.

title: PhySimCode: A Benchmark and Evaluation Method for Physics Video to Code Generation
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "PhySimCode", "input": "2,430 evaluation videos + engine identifier; 162 phenomena", "artifact": "Physical-law/parameter explanation + runnable Python", "checks": "Law correctness/equivalence, execution, parameter recovery and regenerated video similarity", "caveat": "The full described corpus has 160,614 samples; the linked release is the evaluation subset.", "source": "https://github.com/SourajaKundu/PhySimCode"}]
summary: Video plus an engine identifier must yield physical laws, parameters and runnable simulation code. The paper describes 160,614 generated samples; the linked public evaluation release contains 2,430 videos across 162 phenomena.

title: ANTE: Anticipate, Then Execute -- Learning Internal World Models for Coding Agents from Verified Beliefs
summary: Beliefs stated before software actions are settled against real execution, linking predictive world-model supervision to action selection.

title: ExeWorldBench: Benchmarking Code-Based Executable 3D World Modeling
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "ExeWorldBench", "input": "Visual mechanisms, composed systems and high-level physical goals", "artifact": "Code-based executable 3D world", "checks": "Mechanism, compositional and intent-driven executability", "caveat": "These three task levels assess more than render similarity; detailed scoring must follow the source protocol.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15166"}]
summary: Tests mechanism executability, composition of interacting mechanisms, and intent-driven world synthesis. Its organizing question is whether structural and causal understanding becomes working physical interaction.

title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
summary: Different simulation backends expose a common neural-rendering interface; agents improve by distilling experience into inherited playbooks.

title: WorldSolver: Can LLM Agents Simulate the Physical Dynamics via Solver Generation?
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "WorldSolver", "input": "168 tasks from 61 graphics papers across seven physical domains", "artifact": "Solver code completed inside a fixed scaffold", "checks": "Execution checks, visual fidelity and physical plausibility", "caveat": "Solver completion assumes a supplied environment; it is not unrestricted world reconstruction.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08720"}]
summary: Agents must implement numerical solvers inside fixed scaffolds. Executability, rendered behavior and physical plausibility are scored separately.

title: Video2World: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive World Modeling from Embodied Videos
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "Video2World", "input": "222 reconstruction instances from 189 embodied videos", "artifact": "Simulation scene + physical settings + robot behavior", "checks": "Geometric fidelity, dynamic fidelity and functional task correctness", "caveat": "A visually accurate reconstruction can still fail the manipulation task.", "source": "https://aetherlabsai.github.io/Video2World"}]
summary: Video-to-simulation is evaluated as an end-to-end coding task; visual reconstruction quality and successful embodied interaction can diverge.

title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "4DCodeBench", "input": "100 real + 100 synthetic videos", "artifact": "Executable dynamic graphics program", "checks": "Appearance, 2D/3D geometry and motion; synthetic reference-world comparisons", "caveat": "Matching observed dynamics does not uniquely identify the governing mechanism.", "source": "https://github.com/4DCodeBench/4DCodeBench"}]
summary: 200 real and synthetic videos test dynamic inverse graphics through executable programs. Separate geometry and motion metrics expose failures that a convincing static reconstruction can hide.

title: World Editing: Intervening on Executable Worlds at Increasing Depth
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "IGMBench", "input": "110 Minecraft/Terraria editing tasks at four intervention depths", "artifact": "Executable game modification", "checks": "Build/load, behavior, preservation and visual checks; over 1.1K criteria", "caveat": "Successful loading does not imply correct behavior or preservation of unaffected state.", "source": "https://vinesmsuic.github.io/IGMWorld/"}]
summary: 110 Minecraft and Terraria modding tasks evaluate property, entity, dynamics and system interventions. Executability, requested behavior, preservation and visual checks distinguish a working edit from a build that merely loads.

title: Physis-Lang: Self-Evolving Language as a Physical Representation for Video World Model
summary: Physical language is an optimized representation for video generation. It is a useful comparison to executable hypotheses, but does not synthesize an executable world program.

title: Text2Sim: Agentic Physics-Based Simulation Generation with Distilled Expertise
summary: Specialized agents and distilled Debug Cards jointly construct and repair Genesis simulations, including rigid, articulated, deformable and cloth phenomena.

title: Code4Scene: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Constructing and Editing 3D Scenes
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "Code4Scene", "input": "Paper: 190 construction/editing cases, 95 public; repository: 160 construction tasks", "artifact": "Engine-native Unreal scene (.umap)", "checks": "Task fulfillment, artifact integrity, static physical validity, repair and preservation", "caveat": "Paper and repository currently describe different releases; do not mix their sizes or leaderboard scores.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/html/2609.36777v1"}]
summary: Evaluates saved Unreal Engine scenes for task fulfillment, integrity, static physical validity and unintended edits. The paper covers 190 construction/editing cases; the repository currently describes an earlier 160-task construction release.

title: GPUPhysBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Correct and Efficient GPU Physics Simulation
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "GPUPhysBench", "input": "50 specified GPU physics operators/simulators", "artifact": "GPU solver implementation", "checks": "Numerical acceptance checks + runtime relative to expert implementations", "caveat": "Measures implementation correctness and efficiency, not physical-law discovery from observations.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/html/2609.35639v1"}]
summary: 50 GPU physics coding tasks separate numerical correctness from runtime relative to expert implementations. This tests the solver implementation layer, without requiring a model to infer a world from video.

title: WorldAgent: Verification-Guided Agentic Physical World Construction
summary: Verification checks world specifications, geometry and simulation states during construction, turning failed obligations into targeted edits and resimulation.

title: GameDirector: Decoupling Gameplay Logic from Rendering for Player-Configurable Game World Models
summary: A director maintains gameplay state and rules, then guides video rendering with text. Its state-to-pixel interface differs from geometry-conditioned approaches.

title: Code Plans, Diffusion Renders: Open-Ended Generative World Modeling
summary: Coordinated agent roles maintain executable rules and persistent multi-agent evolution while diffusion models supply the perceptual observation layer.

title: BVB: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding via Programmatic Reconstruction in Blender
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "BVB / Blender-VideoBench", "input": "288 indoor videos; agent sees video frames only", "artifact": "Animated Blender scene + camera", "checks": "Dual VQA for retained facts; V-JEPA latent similarity for layout/motion", "caveat": "Video reconstruction scores do not establish contact physics or embodied task success.", "source": "https://yoloytang.me/BVB/"}]
summary: Reconstructs 288 indoor videos as animated Blender scenes under a shared Mini-BVB harness. Dual VQA separates retained spatiotemporal facts from perceptual similarity; camera motion need not imply recovered physical dynamics.

title: Recursive Code World Models: Building Complex Worlds through Recursive Scene Programs
summary: Recursive scene programs allocate local reconstruction loops to unresolved parts, then revisit the whole. Code is used for compositional inverse reconstruction here.

title: Programmable World Model
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "CombatStateBench", "input": "Programmable combat worlds", "artifact": "State-driven interactive visual world", "checks": "Entity count and state accuracy", "caveat": "Count/state fidelity does not exhaust general world intelligence or physical correctness.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10540"}]
summary: An explicit global state includes off-screen entities and non-visual attributes. State-augmented 3D boxes bridge programmable rules and visual observations.

title: VeriPhy: Agentic Physical Reasoning for World Model Evaluation and Refinement
summary: Typed obligations and provenance-carrying measurements support auditable physical judgments, including abstention. This is a verification system, not a simulator.

title: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning
summary: An abductive propose–execute–render–verify loop discovers executable explanations; verified worlds then provide quantitative physical supervision.

title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
summary: A coding agent owns persistent state and consequences; a video model realizes observations from an executable proxy. Distinguish this physical-world framework from Meta's software CWM.

title: VideoCoCo: Code-as-CoT for Physically-Consistent Video Generation via an Agentic Dual-Engine System
summary: Executable Blender code acts as a dense process-level chain of thought before draft-conditioned video editing. A key precursor to code-guided generative world rendering.

title: VisualPatchWorld: Code World Models as Latent Structured Representations for Planning
summary: Active probes select a qualitative dynamics form; parameter fitting makes the resulting executable model useful for model-predictive control.

title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
summary: Specialized agents interact with physics engines through code to coordinate assets, materials, motion, cameras and lighting in dynamic 4D worlds.

title: SimWorlds: A Multi-Agent System for Dynamic 3D Scene Creation
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "4DBuildBench", "input": "Text prompts for dynamic procedural scenes", "artifact": "Editable Blender 4D scene", "checks": "Visual fidelity and physical consistency", "caveat": "Text-to-world construction, not inverse reconstruction from source video.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01766"}]
summary: A staged Blender construction protocol and runtime inspection expose mechanism failures that visual review alone can miss.

title: MPMWorlds: Material-Point-Method Simulations for Inferring and Extrapolating Physical Dynamics
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "MPMWorlds", "input": "2D MPM simulation videos with varying physical side information", "artifact": "Inferred simulation code or video-model continuation", "checks": "Parameter/geometry inference and future physical extrapolation", "caveat": "Inference and extrapolation are distinct; the comparisons concern the stated 2D MPM setting.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01538"}]
summary: The code-versus-diffusion comparison separates inferring material parameters from extrapolating stable dynamics in 2D MPM simulations.

title: 3DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agentic Procedural 3D Modeling Via Code
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "3DCodeBench / 3DCodeArena", "input": "Text and image references", "artifact": "Procedural 3D modeling code", "checks": "Execution and 3D output quality; pairwise human preference in 3DCodeArena", "caveat": "Static asset quality does not by itself establish executable physical dynamics.", "source": "https://www.3dcodebench.com/"}]
summary: Text and image references are translated into procedural 3D code. 3DCodeArena adds human preference judgments; successful rendering can still conceal floating or disconnected geometry. A precursor to the 3DCodeVerse data ecosystem.

title: SceneCode: Executable World Programs for Editable Indoor Scenes with Articulated Objects
summary: Part-wise programs, articulation metadata and a persistent registry make generated indoor assets locally editable and simulator-loadable.

title: SimWorld Studio: Automatic Environment Generation with Evolving Coding Agent for Embodied Agent Learning
summary: An evolving engine-level coding agent exports Gym-style worlds; learner feedback shapes the next curriculum rather than just improving a fixed scene.

title: Code2Worlds: Empowering Coding LLMs for 4D World Generation
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "Code4D", "input": "Text descriptions of 4D worlds", "artifact": "Generated scene code with scripted dynamics", "checks": "Scene generation quality, richness and dynamic fidelity", "caveat": "Visual motion critique is not equivalent to simulator-enforced contact physics.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11757"}]
summary: Dual-stream scene construction and a motion critic extend language-to-code from static scenes to scripted 4D dynamics; simulator readiness is a separate question.

title: Debugging code world models
summary: Execution-state prediction is analyzed for token-budget exhaustion, string-state errors and long-horizon action mistakes.

title: SWE-World: Building Software Engineering Agents in Docker-Free Environments
summary: Learned surrogates predict software execution and test feedback, enabling Docker-free agent optimization. Keep this computational-world meaning distinct from physical simulation.

title: Code World Models for General Game Playing
summary: Natural-language rules and trajectories become transition, legality and termination functions usable by MCTS, including partially observed games.

title: CWM: An Open-Weights LLM for Research on Code Generation with World Models
summary: The model predicts computational environment behavior to improve coding and planning. Here code is the modeled domain, not a generated physical world representation.

title: BlenderGym: Benchmarking Foundational Model Systems for Graphics Editing
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "BlenderGym", "input": "Starting scene script + start/goal images; five editing families", "artifact": "Edited Blender Python script", "checks": "Image/perceptual metrics and geometry distances against the target", "caveat": "Graphics editing and verifier scaling; not a video-to-physical-simulation benchmark.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/html/2504.01786v1"}]
summary: An early code-based graphics editing benchmark: agents modify starting scene scripts to match target images across geometry, placement, blend shape, lighting and material tasks. Generator and verifier scaling are studied separately.

title: FactorSim: Generative Simulation via Factorized Representation
summary: Factored POMDP structure reduces context coupling when generating complete simulator code from language, connecting simulation synthesis to policy transfer.

title: Generating Code World Models with Large Language Models Guided by Monte Carlo Tree Search
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "Code World Models Benchmark (CWMB)", "input": "18 RL environments with descriptions and curated trajectories", "artifact": "Python transition/world model", "checks": "Program synthesis and downstream model-based planning", "caveat": "Transition-model utility is evaluated separately from visual rendering.", "source": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15383"}]
summary: Generate, Improve and Fix search synthesizes Python transition models from descriptions and trajectories, then uses them for efficient model-based planning.

title: PhysDreamer: Physics-Based Interaction with 3D Objects via Video Generation
summary: Video priors help infer material dynamics for interactive objects. This inverse-physics neighbor does not generate symbolic world programs.

title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scene as Blender Code
summary: Scene graphs become Blender Python programs with spatial constraints, visual refinement and reusable script libraries. Generated scenes also guide video synthesis, an earlier code-as-visual-plan route before VideoCoCo.

title: Holodeck: Language Guided Generation of 3D Embodied AI Environments
summary: Language-derived relational constraints and asset placement automate 3D environments. A scene-generation precursor, not evidence of synthesized transition code.

title: RoboGen: Towards Unleashing Infinite Data for Automated Robot Learning via Generative Simulation
summary: The propose–generate–learn loop scales tasks, scenes and supervision for robotic skills, establishing an early generative-simulation learning workflow.

title: World Programs for Model-Based Learning and Planning in Compositional State and Action Spaces
summary: A pre-LLM formulation learns dynamics and available actions as a world program from state transitions for compositional planning.

title: WorldStream: Building 3D Worlds as You Explore
summary: Hierarchical semantic plans feed local procedural generators as exploration expands. Object identities and accepted edits survive geometry unloading. The planner selects structured capabilities; streaming here means world expansion, and code is still announced as coming soon.

title: StreamRender-H3: Interactive Coding Worlds with Real-time Streaming Diffusion Render
summary: A Three.js game engine advances explicit state at a fixed timestep and streams semantic maps into a two-step causal MiniMax-H3 renderer. Engine semantics and reference-image appearance are controlled separately.

title: Streaming Code World Model
summary: A community streaming extension of Code World Model uses causal chunks and four-step distillation. Its README explicitly reports 5.1 seconds per 0.71-second chunk on one H200: streaming does not mean real time.

title: H3 Streaming VAE Decoder: Training-Free Streaming without Future Latents
summary: A training-free causal decoding adaptation emits frames without future latents, using cache reuse and brightness correction. The repository also supports NVIDIA’s distilled StreamRender-H3 decoder. This is a decoder component, with no world state or action dynamics of its own.

title: Code Video Model
benchmark_protocols: [{"name": "CodeVideoBench", "input": "Complex video-generation requests", "artifact": "Code-built previs followed by diffusion video", "checks": "Composition, motion and spatiotemporal control in generated video", "caveat": "Video-generation evaluation does not establish a persistent interactive state machine.", "source": "https://code-video-model.github.io/"}]
summary: Executable Three.js previs controls layout, motion and camera; training-free early-step conditioning preserves proxy structure while releasing its flat appearance. This is a code-to-video pipeline rather than necessarily a live interactive simulator.
